4 April 2007

facts: The appeal is directed against the order dated 18.1.2006 passed by learned Single Judge of the High Court of Delhi in Arbitration Petition No.181 of 2005 whereby learned Single Judge dismissed the application for appointment of Arbitrator.

An application styled u/s.11(5) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 was moved by the Ace Pipeline Contracts Private Limited, the appellant herein, for appointing a retired Judge of the Supreme Court of India to adjudicate the claims and disputes between the parties arising out of the contract between the parties dated 10.06.2002.
The main issue was with regard to interpretation of Cl.91 of the contract which pertains to appointment of arbitrator.

Since some differences arose between the parties with regard to the claim of the appellant, a letter dated 21.7.2005 was written to the Director (Marketing) invoking cl.91 of the agreement and requesting him to refer the matter to arbitration for resolving the differences.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: It was submitted before the High Court that since the appointment of Arbitrator has been made after the filing of the petition by the appellant before the High Court, the Director (Marketing) ceased to have any right to appoint any Arbitrator after expiry of thirty days.
respondent_arguments: The Director (Marketing) received reply to the communication dated 12.8.2005 on 16.8.2005 which was received in the Office on 17.8.2005.
After receiving the communication and all the materials on 17.8.2005, the appointing authority appointed Shri P.S. Bhargava as Arbitrator on 22.8.2005.
court_reasoning: Learned Single Judge after examining the matter came to the conclusion that it cannot be said that the appointing authority did not act with due dispatch.
This may be bona fide error.
holding: The appeal is dismissed with no order as to costs.
